test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following airlines was nationalised in the 1953?

I. Bharat Airways

II. Hyderabad Aviation
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The civil aviation industry in India underwent a major transformation with the passage of the **Air Corporations Act** in **1953**, which led to the **nationalisation** of the entire sector.
 
• Under this **Act**, the **Government of India** decided to merge **eight** existing private airlines into two state-owned autonomous corporations.
 
• The eight airlines involved in the nationalisation process were **Air India**, **Air Services of India**, **Airways (India)**, **Bharat Airways**, **Deccan Airways**, **Himalayan Aviation**, **Indian National Airways**, and **Kalinga Airlines**.
 
• **Statement I**: **Bharat Airways** was one of the major private entities founded by the **Birla Group** in **1945**. It was indeed nationalised in **1953** as part of the merger to form **Indian Airlines**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Statement II**: While **Deccan Airways** (based in Hyderabad) was nationalised, there was no major airline officially recognized as **"Hyderabad Aviation"** among the primary eight companies merged under the **1953 Act**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***
 
• The merger resulted in the creation of **Indian Airlines Corporation** for domestic operations and **Air India International** for overseas services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early History of Aviation**: **J.R.D. Tata**, often called the father of Indian civil aviation, launched **Tata Airlines** in **1932**, which carried mail between **Karachi** and **Bombay**. This company was renamed **Air India** in **1946**.
 
• **Bharat Airways**: Established by **G.D. Birla**, this airline was headquartered in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**). It played a significant role in providing air connectivity in the post-independence era before being absorbed into the public sector.
 
• **The Air Corporations Act, 1953**: This legislation was enacted to ensure the planned and coordinated development of air transport services. It gave the government a **monopoly** over the aviation sector for several decades.
 
• **Liberalization**: The monopoly created by the **1953 Act** lasted until **1994**, when the **Air Corporations (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act** was passed. This allowed private scheduled carriers like **Jet Airways** and **Sahara India** to enter the market again.
 
• **Modern Context**: In **January 2022**, the wheel of history came full circle when **Air India** was officially handed back to the **Tata Group**, marking the end of the era of nationalisation for the flagship carrier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The nationalisation was driven by the need for **financial stability** in the aviation industry, as many private airlines were struggling with high operating costs and low profit margins in the early **1950s**.
 
• The **Indian Airlines Corporation** initially took over the fleet of **74 Douglas DC-3 Dakotas**, **12 Vickers Vikings**, and other aircraft from the nationalised private companies.
 
• The headquarters of **Indian Airlines** was established in **New Delhi**, while **Air India** maintained its primary base in **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**).
